In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53 protein expression status is a significant prognostic factor in patients with NSCLCs that are potentially curatively resection.
the expression of p53 protein is the only one of the three proteins (p16, Rb or p53) studied that is of predictive significance in the prognosis of resected NSLCs.
p16, Rbs and p16/Rbs proteins are not significant prognosticators of NSCLCs, while altered p53 protein status tends to be a negative predictor of survival in NSCLCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p53 protein is the most useful predictor of clinical outcome of NSCLCs.
p16 protein expression is not a useful prognostic factor in resected NSCLS.
the loss of Rb, and to some extent the loss of p53, are important factors in the progression of NSCLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p16 and RB are not predictive of clinical outcome.
the loss of p16 and/or RB is not a significant prognostic factor for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
p53 protein status is a negative prognosticator in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancers.
